title: Compact page indexing and read-amplification reduction for paged KV cache
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: implement a compact page-indexing layer and heuristics to reduce read-amplification when the KV cache is paged out to host memory or swapped on GPU. This ticket captures the design, benchmark plan, and integration steps for a paged/blocked KV cache variant that prioritizes low per-request overhead for continuous-batching workloads while avoiding pathological host<->GPU thrash under bursty sequences.

Background:
- Continuous batching increases token-parallelism, but introduces non-uniform KV access patterns: many short-lived contexts interleaved with occasional long-context queries.
- Our current paged slab allocator exposes high read-amplification: small logical reads map to multiple host pages on spillback, causing ~3-4x extra PCIe transfers for some workloads.
- We need an indexing and prefetch strategy that: 1) compresses mapping metadata, 2) allows fast lookup during token generation, and 3) enables low-latency prefetch hints for batched requests.

Design summary (proposed):
1) Compact page index: maintain a two-level mapping where an in-GPU compact index holds the recent N page entries (N tunable per-device). Each entry is a 48-bit tag + 16-bit flags packed into 64-bit words to minimize footprint. The compact index replaces the full page table lookups for hot working sets.

2) Read-amplification reduction via aligned micro-tiling: when migrating host pages back to GPU, write in micro-tiles (e.g., 4KB tiling aligned to host page boundaries) and record a contiguous run-length encoding in the compact index. Small logical KV reads that fall inside a tile map to a single contiguous transfer instead of multiple discontiguous host reads.

3) Batch-aware prefetch hints: the scheduler aggregates token sequences in the batch planner and emits per-request prefetch hints (prefix-length, likely next-kv-keys window). A lightweight bloom filter per-request will be used to indicate likely hot keys; the prefetcher uses the compact index to decide whether to issue coalesced DMA for contiguous tiles.

4) Graceful fallback & spill smoothing: introduce a short resident hysteresis counter per page entry (3-10 allocations) so pages with intermittent reuse aren't immediately demoted. When device memory pressure rises, the eviction policy prefers low-hysteresis pages and attempts to coalesce co-located tiles to minimize future read-amplification.

Trade-offs considered:
- Index size vs hit-rate: larger compact index reduces host lookups but consumes GPU memory. Default N=8192 chosen after microbenchmarks (see bench notes) to balance 1-2% throughput impact for long sequences.
- Prefetch correctness vs extra bandwidth: aggressive prefetch reduces latency but can waste PCIe bandwidth. We opt for conservative bloom-filter thresholds tuned for 95% precision in production traces.
- Complexity of micro-tiling: adds bookkeeping during migrations and slightly more CPU-side work at spill time; judged acceptable given large reduction in repeated PCIe transfers in tail workloads.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (proto): add compact-index data structure and a host-backed fallback table. Implement simple LRU promotion and eviction. Unit tests for correctness and race conditions.
- Phase 2 (tiling): implement micro-tiling writeback/migration and contiguous-run encoding in index. Add migration-time coalescing logic.
- Phase 3 (prefetch): integrate batch planner hints + bloom filter heuristics. Ensure integration with continuous-batching pipeline and that prefetch requests are rate-limited to respect SLOs.
- Phase 4 (telemetry + tuning): add metrics (index hit-rate, read-amplification ratio, extra PCIe bytes, prefetch precision/recall). Run on trace replay harness and on canary in dedicated cluster.

Benchmarks & success criteria:
- Reduce read-amplification ratio by >= 2x on production trace replays for interactive chat workloads (90th percentile sequences).
- Improve tail latency (p99 token latency) under host-spill scenarios by >= 20% with no >3% throughput regression under steady-state long-context workloads.
- Prefetch should have precision >= 0.90 and recall >= 0.65 on sampled traces.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc draft: drive.google.com/drive/fake/link-kv-compact-index (placeholder)
- Trace harness: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-traces (internal)
- Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/XXXX (TBD)

Open questions and risks:
- How to reconcile compact-index rebuild cost during crash/restart with quick warmup? Proposal: persist minimal MRU snapshot in host-side checkpoint and stream-reroot on startup.
- Worst-case prefetch storms under synchronized batch patterns; guard by global prefetch token bucket.
- Interaction with quantized models that change per-token compute distribution; will validate in Phase 2.

Next steps:
- Split into sub-issues: compact-index impl (this ticket), micro-tiling migration (sub-1), prefetch integration (sub-2). Start prototype run on a 4xA100 canary cluster.
